overall_verdict: Principled rejection of a universal intrinsic selectivity-overpotential-turnover law; retain only conditional transport, conservation, and whole-cell energy relations. Catalyst-specific Pareto frontiers remain unknown.

claims.exact_statement: There is no universal monotone relation between product Faradaic selectivity and local cathodic overpotential across electrochemical catalysts. In the two-pathway model j_i=n_i F k_i^0 exp(beta_i eta) C_s^{m_i}, beta_i=alpha_i n_{e,i}F/(RT), target FE odds obey ln(FE_t/(1-FE_t))=ln(n_t k_t^0/(n_s k_s^0))+(beta_t-beta_s)eta+(m_t-m_s)ln(C_s). Setting beta_t=beta_s and m_t=m_s makes FE_t exactly independent of eta and the common reactant concentration.
assumptions: Steady-state Faradaic current only; no capacitive current in the FE denominator.
The two named products account for all Faradaic current.
Both pathways use the same measured surface reactant concentration C_s and have the displayed power-law rate forms.
The claim rejects universality; it does not assert that selectivity is potential-independent in any specific real catalyst.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_counterexample; no universal law is rejected within the stated model interface
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebraic counterexample is elementary and not claimed as a novel theorem. Source studies support configuration dependence, not a universal inference across catalysts.
claims.costs: For application to a material, acquire local product-specific rate curves, local reactant/pH, catalyst state, and steady FE; an electrode potential alone is insufficient.
claims.falsifier: The explicit equal-slope/equal-order parameter instance falsifies any theorem claimed to hold over this model class. A catalyst-specific relation requires testing on held-out potentials and transport conditions.
claims.next_gate: Freeze a model fit on a small equipotential Cu coupon, then test sector-resolved FE and partial currents on larger electrodes at changed collector pitch and flow.

claims.exact_statement: For first-order target kinetics r=k_0 exp(alpha n_e F eta/(RT)) C_s coupled to steady planar transport k_m(C_b-C_s)=r, j=n_p F r obeys j=j_lim k/(k_m+k), j_lim=n_p F k_m C_b, and the apparent Tafel slope is b_app=(2.303 RT/(alpha n_e F))/(1-j/j_lim).
assumptions: Steady planar boundary layer with one dissolved limiting reactant.
First-order surface kinetics in C_s and a cathodic Tafel regime.
Constant k_m, temperature, active catalyst state, and no other substrate source or inhibition.
n_e is the electron count in the potential-sensitive elementary step; n_p is the full product electron stoichiometry.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a Koutecky-Levich/series-rate correction and not claimed as new. It is an explanatory model, not a substitute for porous-electrode transport measurements.
claims.costs: Measure a transport-limited current under the same geometry and feed. Near j_lim, uncertainty in j_lim sharply amplifies corrected intrinsic-current uncertainty.
claims.falsifier: Within the stated single-reaction model, measured j(eta) that violates the relation after independently measuring k_m, C_b, and kinetic parameters falsifies the model assumptions or implementation.
claims.next_gate: Measure product-specific local Tafel curves below and near the limiting current at two independently measured k_m values.

claims.exact_statement: If product t consumes nu_t molecules of a limiting reactant per molecule and its FE is defined against total steady Faradaic current, then j_t <= n_t F J_X,max/nu_t and j_total <= n_t F J_X,max/(nu_t FE_t).
assumptions: The maximum reactant supply J_X,max is measured per geometric electrode area under operating conditions.
No uncounted source or reservoir supplies the reactant.
Steady-state product rate and total Faradaic current use the same sampling interval.
All reactant replenishment from gas, dissolved feed, and carbonate/bicarbonate is included in J_X,max when relevant.
claims.novelty_boundary: Direct material balance; not claimed as novel. The unresolved experimental quantity is the effective maximum flux in porous or buffer-fed electrodes.
claims.costs: Needs calibrated inlet/outlet flow and composition, product assay, total current, carbonate crossover, and gas/liquid mass balance.
claims.falsifier: A sustained target molar production rate above J_X,max/nu_t with a complete, calibrated reactant balance falsifies the claimed flux bound or its measurement assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Acquire J_X,max and carbon balance in the same GDE used for FE measurements, rather than infer it from bulk dissolved CO2 alone.

claims.exact_statement: At steady full-cell voltage V_cell, total current density j, electrode area A, product electron stoichiometry n_i, and product FE_i=n_i F dot(n_i)/(jA), stack electrical energy per mole of product is w_i=n_i F V_cell/FE_i. Between two designs with unchanged product thermodynamics and no auxiliaries, energy per mole improves exactly when FE_i,2/FE_i,1 > V_cell,2/V_cell,1.
assumptions: The measured voltage is the full cell voltage over the same interval as FE and product rate.
Product FE accounts for total Faradaic charge and product losses/crossover are measured correctly.
Auxiliary power, feed conditioning, heating, pumping, separation, and recycle are excluded from this stack-only identity.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Faraday and power accounting; not claimed as a new result. Its practical use is to compare FE gain against full-cell voltage cost consistently.
claims.costs: Requires two-electrode cell voltage, product-specific calibrated flow/concentration, total current, and a declared system-energy boundary.
claims.falsifier: A complete steady-state charge/product/voltage balance that violates w_i=n_i F V_cell/FE_i falsifies the measurement definitions or accounting boundary.
claims.next_gate: Report full-cell V and product FE together for each operating point; add pump, gas, heat, and separation power before system-level energy claims.

claims.exact_statement: For a thin resistive catalyst sheet with uniform normal current density j, thickness t, and resistivity rho, one-edge collection over length L gives a maximum in-plane voltage drop rho j L^2/(2t). Equipotential conductors at pitch s give a between-conductor maximum drop rho j s^2/(8t), hence the ideal maximum-drop ratio is s^2/(4L^2).
assumptions: Quasi-steady one-dimensional sheet conduction with uniform current source.
Constant sheet resistivity and thickness.
Perfectly equipotential edge/wires and no current redistribution feedback.
claims.status: internally_derived_conditional_sheet_model; direction supported by source-reported spatial model/experiment
claims.novelty_boundary: The scaling follows Ohm's law and is not claimed as new. Real current varies with potential; the cited authors solve a nonlinear field numerically.
claims.costs: Measure in-plane sheet resistance and current distribution; large cells require high-current hardware, spatial voltage taps, and segmented product sampling.
claims.falsifier: A constant-resistivity uniform-current sheet with measured geometry violating the derived ratio falsifies the sheet model or measurement. A real electrode can deviate if its current is nonuniform.
claims.next_gate: Test the s^2 reduction with 4-, 10-, and 20-mm collector pitches and held-out sector FE.

claims.exact_statement: Recent primary studies report device- and microenvironment-dependent co-variation of potential/cell voltage, partial current, Faradaic selectivity, and transport; these source-reported observations show that empirical trends are configuration-specific but do not certify a universal law.
assumptions: Published measurement definitions and experimental controls are as reported by each source.
Values are not independently reproduced in this research track.
claims.novelty_boundary: No new experimental finding, reproduction, or priority claim is made. HCGDE 50-cm2 trials were single experiments and non-isothermal numerical details need supplement-level recheck before reproduction.
claims.costs: Reproduction needs electrochemical cell hardware, matched cathodes, gas/liquid product analytics, local potential/pH probes, and replicate/stability runs.
claims.falsifier: Direct replication under the published controls fails to reproduce the reported current, FE, and voltage changes within the reported experimental variability.
claims.next_gate: Run a replicated segmented-cell intervention with matched catalyst, flow, local potential, pH/CO2, and source-resolved energy accounting.
